1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`

  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position

  mouseup [button]            press mouse up

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:

  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file

  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie

- Complete “The Little Things” as a playable game and verify gameplay.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For check screenshots, use JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail requires it.

## Decisions
- No gameplay changes have been identified as necessary so far.

## Work State
### Completed
- Advanced through Mara’s opening dialogue to the watch inspection and verified the watch’s dial and crown details.
- Turned the watch over and verified its engraving and seam details; closing the inspection and satchel overlays works when closed in that order.
- Verified that discovering the engraving and seam updates the thought text and persists; the journal displays discovered notes.
- Confirmed the scene responds to clicking: clicking the counter opens its dialogue.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Continue exploring clue collection and progression through the game.
- Inspect the active dialogue and determine a gameplay path forward; the latest click opened “The counter” dialogue.
- Investigate the two browser console errors, previously observed as `/favicon.ico` 404s.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Close the counter dialogue and continue exploring scene hotspots and interactions.
2. Collect clues and test progression through the remaining story, watching for gameplay blockers.
3. Check browser console errors; if changes are made, rerun relevant checks and summarize verification and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and screens.
- `js/game.js`: Game engine, input, overlays, and UI wiring.
- `js/data.js`: Story, world, dialogue, and object hotspot definitions.
- `js/core.js`: Utilities, save, and audio.
- `js/scenes-a.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/scenes-b.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/art.js`: Watch/object drawing.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Game is running at `http://localhost:3002`.

- Latest browser state is the counter dialogue: “The counter is where the shop does its thinking. A brass bell, a ledger, a lamp with a crooked shade.”

- Complete “The Little Things” as a playable game and verify gameplay.

- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For check screenshots, use JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail requires it.

## Decisions
- No gameplay code changes have been identified as necessary so far.

## Work State

### Completed
- Advanced Mara’s opening dialogue; inspected the watch face, crown, engraving, and seam.
- Verified discovered clues persist and appear in the journal; scene hotspots respond to interaction.
- Exited the shop to Chapel Lane, met Wren, and explored her conversation.
- Raised the watch with Wren; obtained the 1962 photograph, journal details, and photo clues.
- Inspected the photograph’s front-side details and closed the inspection.
- Followed the station clue to Harrowmere Station; verified the scene loads and movement works.

- Explore station hotspots and continue story progression; then explore the remaining locations and test the full game.
- Recheck the two browser console errors, previously identified as `/favicon.ico` 404s.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Explore station hotspots, including the timetable and June, following the 8:17 clue.
2. Continue through the clock shop and remaining locations; verify progression and ending.
3. Recheck console errors; if changes are made, rerun relevant checks and summarize verification and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and screens.
- `js/game.js`: Game engine, input, overlays, and UI wiring.
- `js/data.js`: Story, world, dialogue, and object hotspot definitions.
- `js/core.js`: Utilities, save, and audio.
- `js/scenes-a.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/scenes-b.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/art.js`: Watch/object drawing.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Game is running at `http://localhost:3002`.

- No code changes have been made.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Little Things” as a playable game and verify gameplay through its ending.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For check screenshots, use JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail requires it.

## Decisions
- No gameplay code changes have been identified as necessary so far.

## Work State

### Completed
- Advanced Mara’s opening dialogue; inspected the watch face, crown, engraving, and seam.
- Verified discovered clues persist and appear in the journal; scene hotspots respond to interaction.
- Exited the shop to Chapel Lane, met Wren, and explored her conversation.
- Raised the watch with Wren; obtained the 1962 photograph, journal details, and photo clues.
- Followed the station clue to Harrowmere Station; verified the scene loads and movement works.
- Interacted with station objects, inspected the timetable, and discovered `timetable_817`, `timetable_note`, and `timetable_last`; confirmed clue, discovery, and timetable card persistence.
- Spoke with June, showed her the photograph, and obtained her account, platform ticket, and clues `june_account`, `ticket_punch`, and `ticket_date`.
- Explored June’s “Why didn’t you go after him?” response.

### Active
- Continue story progression: take the watch to Theo, uncover the letter and ledger clues, connect the clue-board threads, and reach an ending.
- Recheck console errors, including the previously observed `/favicon.ico` 404s.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue with June’s remaining dialogue topics as desired, then leave the station and follow the watch clue to Theo on Chapel Lane.
2. Open and inspect the watch, investigate the letter and repair ledger, and solve the clue-board connections.
3. Return to June and make the watch decision; verify the ending and any post-ending content.
4. Recheck console errors; if changes are made, rerun relevant checks and summarize verification and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and screens.
- `js/game.js`: Game engine, input, overlays, and UI wiring.
- `js/data.js`: Story, world, dialogue, and object hotspot definitions.
- `js/core.js`: Utilities, save, and audio.
- `js/scenes-a.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/scenes-b.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/art.js`: Watch/object drawing.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Game URL: `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Save is stored in localStorage under `littlethings.save.v2`; current scene is `station`, and June’s dialogue overlay is open on her platform-ticket line.
- Flags include `metWren`, `photoFound`, `timetableFound`, `metJune`, and `juneStory`; the watch, photo, and ticket are acquired.
- Timetable clues and June’s ticket/account clues are recorded; `letterFound` is still false and no ending is set.
- No code changes have been made.
- Playwright snapshot reported one console error; its details have not been inspected.

## Objective
- Complete “The Little Things” as a playable game and verify gameplay through its ending.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For check screenshots, use JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail requires it.

## Decisions
- No gameplay code changes have been identified as necessary so far.

## Work State

### Completed
- Advanced Mara’s opening dialogue; inspected the watch face, crown, engraving, and seam.
- Verified discovered clues persist and appear in the journal; scene hotspots respond to interaction.
- Exited the shop to Chapel Lane, met Wren, and explored her conversation.
- Raised the watch with Wren; obtained the 1962 photograph, journal details, and photo clues.
- Followed the station clue to Harrowmere Station; verified the scene loads and movement works.
- Interacted with station objects, inspected the timetable, and discovered `timetable_817`, `timetable_note`, and `timetable_last`; confirmed clue, discovery, and timetable card persistence.
- Spoke with June, showed her the photograph, and obtained her account, platform ticket, and clues `june_account`, `ticket_punch`, and `ticket_date`.
- Explored June’s “Why didn’t you go after him?” and “I’m sorry.” dialogue.
- Left the station for Chapel Lane and entered the clock shop; confirmed movement and scene transition work.

### Active
- Speak with Theo, open the watch, and discover the letter and repair ledger clues.
- Connect the clue-board threads, return to June, make the watch decision, and verify an ending and post-ending content.
- Recheck console errors, including the previously observed `/favicon.ico` 404.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue from Marchetti & Son, where the player is in the clock shop; interact with Theo and the workbench to pursue the watch, letter, and ledger.
2. Solve the clue-board connections and follow the resulting story prompts.
3. Return to June, make the watch decision, and verify the ending and any post-ending content.
4. Recheck console errors; if changes are made, rerun relevant checks and summarize verification and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and screens.
- `js/game.js`: Game engine, input, overlays, and UI wiring.
- `js/data.js`: Story, world, dialogue, and object hotspot definitions.
- `js/core.js`: Utilities, save, and audio.
- `js/scenes-a.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/scenes-b.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/art.js`: Watch/object drawing.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Game URL: `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Save is stored in localStorage under `littlethings.save.v2`; current scene is `clock`, with the player at approximately `{x: 863.5, y: 806.9}`. No dialogue overlay is open.
- Flags include `metWren`, `photoFound`, `timetableFound`, `metJune`, and `juneStory`; the watch, photo, and ticket are acquired.
- Timetable clues and June’s ticket/account clues are recorded; `letterFound` is still false and no ending is set.
- No code changes have been made.
- A console error was observed for `http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico`.

### Result
"Theo Marchetti

CLOCK REPAIRER

×

The unsent letter
×

CLICK THE SMALL WARM GLIMMERS

One sheet of thin paper, folded down to the size of a thumbnail. The creases are soft. There is a cornflower pressed in the middle.

The first line

“Dear June. I have started this letter eleven times.” The paper is thin, folded small enough to fit inside a watch case.

The cornflower

A cornflower, pressed flat between the folds. Blue as a September evening. It has been waiting in the dark, patient as a stopped watch.

The middle

“My father is ill. The doctor says weeks, then says months, then stops saying anything at all. I could not leave him, and I could not ask you to stay. I got as far as the bridge and turned back.”

The signature

“I heard the 8:17 go. I am sorry I was not braver. I will not send this.” It is signed Elias. The ink is steady.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete “The Little Things” as a playable game and verify gameplay through its ending.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For check screenshots, use JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail requires it.

## Decisions
- No gameplay code changes have been identified as necessary so far.

## Work State

### Completed
- Advanced Mara’s opening dialogue; inspected the watch face, crown, engraving, and seam.
- Verified discovered clues persist and appear in the journal; scene hotspots respond to interaction.
- Exited the shop to Chapel Lane, met Wren, and explored her conversation.
- Raised the watch with Wren; obtained the 1962 photograph, journal details, and photo clues.
- Followed the station clue to Harrowmere Station; verified scene loads and movement works.
- Interacted with station objects and timetable; discovered `timetable_817`, `timetable_note`, and `timetable_last`, and confirmed clue, discovery, and timetable card persistence.
- Spoke with June, showed her the photograph, and obtained her account, platform ticket, and clues `june_account`, `ticket_punch`, and `ticket_date`; explored additional dialogue.
- Entered Marchetti & Son, spoke with Theo, and opened the watch.
- Obtained and inspected the unsent letter; verified letter and repair-ledger clues/cards persist, including `letter_opening`, `letter_reason`, `letter_signature`, `letter_flower`, `ledger_entry`, and `ledger_margin`.
- Connected all four essential clue-board threads (`d1`–`d4`).
- Opened the counter decision and chose “RETURN THEM”; verified the “The hour kept” ending.
- Continued into post-ending content; verified the epilogue loads at the shop with ending `returned` and the watch/letter removed from inventory.

### Active
- Verify post-ending conversations/content with Mara, Wren, June, and others as practical.
- Recheck console errors, including the previously observed `/favicon.ico` 404.
- Summarize verification and assumptions when complete.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Explore post-ending dialogue and any remaining epilogue interactions.
2. Recheck console errors.
3. If checks reveal issues, make targeted changes and rerun relevant checks; otherwise report completion and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and screens.
- `js/game.js`: Game engine, input, overlays, and UI wiring.
- `js/data.js`: Story, world, dialogue, clue-board connections, and object hotspots.
- `js/core.js`: Utilities, save, and audio.
- `js/scenes-a.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/scenes-b.js`: Scene rendering.
- `js/art.js`: Watch/object drawing.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Game URL: `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Save is stored in localStorage under `littlethings.save.v2`; current scene is `shop`, after continuing from the ending.
- Ending is `returned`; epilogue and ending-seen flags are set. The watch and letter were removed from inventory; photo and ticket remain.
- Four essential deductions are recorded: `d1`, `d2`, `d3`, and `d4`.
- No code changes have been made.
- A console/resource error was previously observed for `http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico`.
